reported_claims.text: Ugandan forces will soon withdraw from Lubero; militia forces, including some apparently allied to the Congolese government, have stepped up attacks on civilians in Ituri and North Kivu.

reported_claims.text: Army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba threatened on X to take control of Walikale and called for the unconditional surrender of the airport in Isiro.
The DRC summoned Uganda's head of mission, calling the remarks particularly serious.

location: North Kivu and Ituri, eastern DR Congo
title: Uganda to pull troops from Lubero as row with DR Congo over army chief's threats escalates
observed_action: Uganda's army said on 27 November it would soon withdraw forces from Lubero, North Kivu, after army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba threatened on 23 November to take Walikale and demanded the surrender of Isiro airport; Kinshasa summoned Uganda's head of mission.
interpretation: A deterioration in Uganda-DRC military cooperation against the ADF that could open space for armed groups and the FRN (formerly M23) offensive toward Walikale. Assessment, not confirmed intent.
summary: Uganda's army said it would soon withdraw troops from Lubero in eastern DR Congo, accusing militias, including some apparently allied to the Congolese government, of attacks on civilians. The announcement follows posts by Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba threatening to take Walikale and calling for the surrender of Isiro airport, which led the DRC to summon Uganda's head of mission.
impact_assessment: Potential: weakened operations against the IS-linked ADF, a security vacuum in Lubero, and a risk of direct Uganda-DRC tension alongside the FRN offensive.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: an official troop withdrawal and diplomatic rupture in an active conflict zone; no clashes between the two states reported.
monitoring_actions: Track UPDF deployments in North Kivu and Ituri

sources.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from eastern DR Congo town amid diplomatic spat
